description: PHP regular expressions beside the JSON Schema pattern PatternTranslation::ecma() makes of each (null when it leaves pattern out), and values with whether PHP's preg_match accepts them. PatternUnderUnicodeTest asserts both columns in PHP; the React app's Vitest (src/test/patternEngines.test.ts) reads the same rows with an ECMA engine: a carried pattern accepts every value PHP accepts, and a row left out holds a value PHP accepts that the body read by ECMA would refuse.

rows.why: With u, PCRE's \d takes in every decimal digit; ECMA's is 0-9.
With u, PCRE's \w takes in every letter; ECMA's is ASCII.
With u, PCRE reads a letter outside ASCII as a word character, so a boundary stands before it; ECMA sees none.
ECMA's \s holds the no-break space, so its [^\s] leaves out what PCRE's keeps.
Without u, PCRE's negated class matches one byte of a character outside ASCII.
With u, PCRE's \s holds U+0085 and U+180E, which ECMA's lacks.
Without u, both read \w as A-Z, a-z, 0-9 and _.
Without u, \d inside a class is 0-9 in both.
Without u, both find a boundary by ASCII word characters, and a byte of a character outside ASCII is none.
Without u, PCRE's \s is six ASCII characters, all of them in ECMA's, which is wider.
